summary: Renewal check-in covering SkyTech's upcoming renewal in May; customer is interested in adding two additional dedicated GPU units, enabling EU-region capacity, and evaluating Private deployment for data residency. Security team raised SOC2/KMS questions. Redwood will provide updated pricing and benchmarks; next steps agreed.
topics: Private deployment / VPC for data residency
transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Rao (Redwood CSM); Leah Ortiz (SkyTech CTO), Mark Benson (Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Security), Ethan Wu (SRE)

AUTO SUMMARY:
- Quick renewal check, SkyTech aims to increase reserved capacity and add EU region.
- Security wants Private/VPC options and SOC2/KMS assurances.
- Redwood to send updated pricing and benchmark artifacts; schedule Private demo in staging.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Leah (SkyTech): Leah here.
[00:07] Mark (SkyTech): Mark on infra.
[00:09] Priya (SkyTech): Priya, security.
[00:11] Ethan (SkyTech): Ethan, SRE.
[00:13] Jonah (Redwood): Jonah here.
[00:15] Aisha (Redwood): Aisha here.
[00:18] Maya: Cool. So main agenda, renewal in May, expansion asks — more capacity and an EU region, and Priya had some questions about Private deployment. We want to keep this pretty pragmatic — confirm constraints, timeline, and next steps.

[02:05] Leah: Sounds good. For context, we've been happy with the uptime and the latency overall, but the last month we've seen some tail latency spikes during batch processing and we're hitting our committed qps in afternoons. That's why we're looking at adding 2 more dedicated GPUs and maybe enabling EU region for our EU customers.

[03:12] Mark: Yeah, especially for analytics workloads where sequence lengths are larger, the cost per token is fine but latency variance matters. We want to avoid moving traffic to US region for EU users.

[04:20] Maya: Got it. Jonah, did you see the logs we shared from the POC? The KV cache hit patterns looked like...
[04:30] Jonah: Yeah I looked through them; there's a mix of short conversational calls and long-prompt batch jobs. The POC config we used had conservative batching to preserve latency, so cpu/gpu utilization wasn't fully saturated — there's headroom but the tail latencies come from occasional long sequences and cache misses.

[05:40] Priya: On our side, the security team is leaning towards Private or at least VPC peering for anything that handles EU PII. SOC2 is assumed but we need specifics: do you support CMKs in KMS, audit logs retention, and can we control key rotation?

[06:05] Maya: Short answer: yes, we support customer-managed keys (KMS) in Private and Dedicated setups, and audit logs are available; retention and rotation policies are configurable depending on plan. We'll share the SOC2 pack and our KMS integration docs after this call.

[07:20] Priya: Great. Also need to know about data residency for embeddings — do you persist embeddings outside the customer's region?

[07:35] Jonah: With our Dedicated/EU region option, embeddings and KV cache stay in-region for the request flow; for Hosted customers we have configurable retention — but for Private you control storage. We'll send the architecture diagram that shows where caches and stores live.

[09:00] Leah: Timeline-wise: our contract renews May 15. We're evaluating whether to extend current reserved capacity and add the two GPUs now as a top-up, or renegotiate the annual commit. What's the recommended path?

[09:25] Maya: Two practical paths: 1) Short-term top-up: add +2 GPUs to your Dedicated pool effective immediately and prorate billing through the renewal — fastest. 2) Recommit: update annual reserved capacity and pricing, which gets you better unit pricing but requires sign-off. We can do a blended quote too.

[10:18] Mark: For procurement, a single amendment for the top-up is easier; finance prefers not to renegotiate the whole contract unless the price is compelling.

[11:02] Maya: Understood. We'll prepare both options: a prorated top-up quote and a renewal quote with the updated commit and EU region pricing. Expect both by Monday.

[12:00] Ethan: For the EU region, is there an incremental latency penalty for cross-region routing or auto failover? We care about 95th/99th percentiles.

[12:18] Jonah: If you enable EU region and route EU traffic there, latency is comparable to US region for EU customers — the main advantage is avoiding the transatlantic hop. For failover we can route to US as a fallback which adds e.g., 60–120ms depending on route. For 99th percentile, we'd want dedicated capacity in EU to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

[13:55] Priya: On encryption at rest and in transit, do you support TLS 1.3 for in-transit, and are logs encrypted at rest? Also, any third-party subprocessor list?

[14:20] Maya: Yes TLS1.3 in-transit. Logs and storage are encrypted at rest. We'll attach our security/compliance pack with subprocessors list.

[15:30] Leah: Another ask: can we get a short benchmark that matches our worst-case prompt profile — long sequences, batch size ~8 — so procurement can see cost/latency numbers?

[15:45] Jonah: Yep, I can re-run the POC benchmark with those parameters on a dedicated EU replica and output 50/95/99 latency and token-cost per 1M tokens. I'll also include config (quantization, batch settings, kernel choices) we used.

[17:10] Mark: One minor point, on autoscaling during nightly jobs: sometimes autoscale latency causes mid-job throttling. Can you confirm warm pools or burst capacity options?

[17:28] Maya: We offer reserved capacity with burst credits and warm-pool options on Dedicated; we can include a policy suggestion to keep two GPUs warm during nightly windows. That helps avoid cold-starts.

[18:55] Leah: Good. About Private deployment — cost wise, what's the delta compared to Dedicated? And operationally, how much runbook support do you provide?

[19:15] Maya: Private is higher fixed cost because you get a private control plane and more operational overhead; pricing depends on scale and support tier. Operationally we provide a managed private control plane, a runbook, and options for 24/7 support as an add-on. We'll outline a rough TCO in the renewal quote.

[20:40] Priya: If we go Private, how does key management work with our HSM? Can we integrate with an on-prem HSM or do you require cloud KMS?

[21:00] Jonah: We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS for cloud deployments. For on-prem/air-gapped Private, we have integrations for bring-your-own-HSM via standard KMIP or a proxy layer; we'll need to scope network connectivity and key provisioning. That's more of a technical deep dive — we can schedule a separate session.

[22:35] Maya: Let's flag a technical deep dive for Priya and Ethan; Jonah can lead that with our infra security engineer. Tentative: next Friday.

[23:12] Priya: Yes please. Also, we need the SOC2 attestation and pen-test summary.

[23:20] Maya: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and recent pentest exec summary in the follow-up email.

[24:45] Leah: For procurement, what approvals do you need to include EU region in the contract? Any regulatory stuff?

[25:05] Maya: Mostly an addendum specifying region and data residency terms; we also include subprocessors and DPA clauses. If you have specific EU data residency contract language, send it over and we'll include it.

[26:40] Ethan: On the implementation timeline, if we approve the top-up today, how fast can Redwood enable the EU region?

[26:55] Jonah: If Dedicated capacity is available in EU, we can spin up within 3–5 business days; if we need to provision new hardware, it could be a couple of weeks. I'll check capacity and note it in the quote.

[28:10] Mark: Can you also include an example traffic-splitting policy so we can gradually shift EU traffic?

[28:20] Jonah: Yes — we have routing policy templates (latency-based, geo-preferred, weighted) and a canary rollout pattern. I'll include examples.

[29:33] Maya: Quick commercial check — Leah, are you leaning towards top-up + separate renewal negotiation later, or a single commit now?

[29:45] Leah: Leaning to top-up now to get EU capacity quickly and then revisit the renewal with usage numbers. Procurement wants the top-up amendment.

[30:10] Maya: Ok we'll prioritize the prorated top-up quote and include the renewal option as a second doc.

[31:20] Aisha (CSM): I'll draft a pilot extension doc for the two additional GPUs so we can track objectives and success metrics.

[31:40] Priya: On metrics, we need SLOs for 95th and 99th latency plus data access logs and retention window.

[32:05] Jonah: We'll map Redwood metrics to your SLOs; 95th is usually straightforward with dedicated pools, 99th depends on avoiding cache misses and reserved capacity. We'll include mitigation strategies.

[33:50] Leah: Anything else we should cover?

[34:00] Ethan: One question — any vendor lock-in on model variants if we pin a model version?

[34:12] Jonah: No vendor lock-in — you can pin model versions and we support rollbacks and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants. If you want to migrate to Private later, model artifacts can be exported under the terms in the contract.

[35:20] Mark: Procurement will want a line-item for EU region ops costs; please make that explicit.

[35:32] Maya: Will do. We'll break out costs: additional GPUs, EU region premium, private deployment delta, and support tiers.

[36:50] Leah: Good. I think that's the bulk. Recap please?

[36:58] Maya: Recap: 1) Redwood to send prorated top-up quote for +2 GPUs and EU region pricing; 2) include alternate renewal quote; 3) Jonah to rerun POC benchmark with your worst-case prompt profile and share configs; 4) security pack (SOC2, KMS docs, subprocessors) to Priya; 5) schedule technical deep dive for Private/HSM integration; 6) Aisha to prepare pilot extension doc. Anyone object?

[38:05] Leah: All good.
[38:10] Priya: Sounds good.
[38:12] Mark: Good.
[38:20] Maya: Great — we'll follow up via email with artifacts and dates.

[39:30] Aisha: I'll create the calendar invites for the deep dive and demo pro tem.
[39:50] Jonah: I'll start the benchmark run today and share interim results.

[40:20] Priya: Expecting compliance items by end of week.

[41:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll talk soon.
[41:05] Leah: Thanks all, bye.
